items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Stecklet Interview, 1959-06-15
items.q: But the best trombone player that I ever heard was a fella by the name of Ricky Tom.

ctx.x: In this brass band again, you say three cornets and clarinet, how many trombones? Well, one.

One? One. Just one. Now, of course, they had valve trombone or sliding trombone, and they had valve trombone. Now, Mr. Mallow from down below, his brother used to be a valve trombone player. But he was good, but he never read nothing. But he had a good ear. You could take that fella and you played a piece once, and the next time you played it, he had a down pat, and he could come right in there with his trombone parts, mighty good. But the best trombone player that I ever heard was a fella by the name of Ricky…

get another beer and get another sandwich because I know fellas wake up in that section. Not only ponds, but fellas wake up that way and they used to go there and get their lunch and drink beer with their lunch for ten cents and have all they want to eat. Of course those days have gone by forever.
